name: Phone P009 export privacy mutation guard
command: scripts/mutation-probe.sh --file '${PHONE_APP_ROOT}/packages/data/src/postgres-store.ts' --mutate 's/callContentExport\(toCall\(row\), row.segments, row.voicemail\)/({ format: "papercusp-phone-call-v1", call: toCall(row), segments: row.segments, voicemail: row.voicemail })/' --test 'test -f "{}" && cd '\''${PHONE_APP_ROOT}/packages/data'\'' && npm test -- src/call-export.integration.test.ts' --relocation overlay --expect caught
summary: Maintained copy-out overlay guard ran the registered export integration suite against canonical and relocated canonical snapshots (9 pass each), then a PostgreSQL export mutant that returned the persisted call without its privacy allowlist. The guard caught the private recordingUri at the intended assertion (8 pass, 1 intentional failure). This verifies software falsifiability; no public PSTN, policy approval or shipment.

assertions.evidence: Both baseline executions reported 9 passed, 0 failed in call-export.integration.test.ts.
Exact failure: call export (postgres) > exports ordered content and read state without private media or conversation authority; AssertionError: expected { …(14) } to not have property "recordingUri".

MUTATION_PROBE_RESULT verdict=caught expected=caught target=copy-out baseline_exit=0 guard_exit=1 mutant_parse=unchecked assertion_evidence=vitest-failed-tests relocation=overlay; wrapper exit 0 after canonical-byte restoration verification. No tracked file was mutated.
